articles.title: Pennywise returns in the first trailer for HBO’s It prequel Welcome to Derry
articles.summary: The It duology from 2017 is getting a TV prequel It: Welcome to Derry directed by Andy Muschietti with Bill Skarsgard returning as Pennywise the clown.
articles.body: It: Welcome to Derry, the prequel TV show for Stephen King’s It, has a new trailer. Coming to HBO Max (née Max, née HBO Go, née HBO Now, née…) this fall, the show centers on what seems to be the origins of It’s supernatural villain Pennywise the Clown and the first crop of kids to ever take him down. In the trailer, we’re introduced to an African American family moving into Derry, Maine where they face a chilly reception from the town’s white residents. The family’s child makes friends with other local kids and together they start experiencing then investigating strange events in the town related to children gone missing. Set in Maine in 1962, Welcome to Derry functions as a prequel to the It remake duology released in 2017. Andy Muschietti, director of the two It films, is the writer for Welcome to Derry and will direct a number of the series’ episodes. Bill Skarsgard is also returning to reprise his role as Pennywise.

articles.title: Jamshedpur police arrest 15 for gambling, seize cash and phones
articles.summary: Jamshedpur police arrest 15 in Prakash Nagar gambling raid; seize 16 smartphones, Rs 7.67 lakh cash, cards; DC orders tougher anti-drug action, hotspot surveillance.
articles.body: Jamshedpur: A total of 15 people were arrested on charges of gambling from a house located in Prakash Nagar under the Birsanagar police station limits on Monday. A total of 16 smartphones, Rs 7,67,400 in cash, and several decks of playing cards were seized during the operation, police said.Attending a Narcotics Coordination Committee (NCORD) meeting earlier in the day, East Singhbhum deputy commissioner (DC) Rajiv Ranjan directed police and departments concerned to step up action against drug trafficking and strengthen surveillance in identified narcotics hotspots.“Strict legal action must be taken against those involved in drug trafficking and illegal drug trade. Sensitive areas should be monitored regularly, and there should be no unnecessary delays in investigations or legal proceedings. All departments concerned must work in coordination to identify and dismantle drug networks operating in the district,” DC Ranjan said.Enforcement and monitoring were under way at 10 hotspots. In September, action under the NDPS Act led to the seizure of 133 kg ganja and 52 packets of brown sugar, officials said.The education department and local police stations were directed to continue anti-drug programmes in schools. “Anti-drug awareness programmes should be conducted regularly in schools and colleges to educate students about the harmful effects of drugs on health, families and society,” DC stated.Urging residents to report narcotics sale on helpline 112 or police control room 0657-2431028, the DC stressed that de-addiction, treatment and rehabilitation services must remain accessible and effective for people affected by substance abuse.Stay updated with the latest Ranchi news. articles.title: Rs 799 kurti that never came, but led cops to Rs 30-crore cyber frauds
articles.summary: Delhi Police cracked a Rs 30-crore cyber fraud network after a DU student’s Rs 799 kurti order led to multiple payments; seven arrested, devices seized.
articles.body: New Delhi: A routine online shopping order for a kurti worth Rs 799 led Delhi Police to unearth an alleged cyber fraud syndicate that channelled credit transactions worth over Rs 30 crore through a network of bank accounts. Seven people have been arrested.The probe began after a student of Delhi University’s Ramjas College was allegedly cheated of Rs 6,450 by an online seller who repeatedly demanded payments on the pretext of facilitating a parcel delivery. Following an analysis of nearly 200 mobile numbers and IMEIs, police traced the money trail to Greater Noida and Kanpur. Police have linked 27 cyber fraud complaints from different states to the network.The student had come across an advertisement for a kurti on a social media platform. She was redirected to WhatsApp, where she placed an order worth Rs 799 and paid Rs 400 in advance through a QR code. She later received a call for a passcode for delivery. On contacting the seller, she was allegedly induced to pay Rs 1,150 as a refundable charge for generating the code, followed by payments of Rs 2,000, Rs 2,650 and Rs 650 on similar pretexts. The parcel never arrived and no money was refunded, police said.DCP (north) Niharika Bhatt said investigators analysed banking transactions and digital records obtained from companies. The cheated amount was traced through a merchant account to a bank account linked to a firm in Greater Noida.Sustained surveillance led to coordinated raids in Greater Noida on Oct 16, resulting in the arrest of Aditya Mishra (23), Ayush Verma (22), Abhishek Pal (23), Himanshu Rana (29), Rahul Kumar (30) and Gaurav Pandey (24). Udit Pratap Singh Bhadauriya (22) was arrested in Kanpur on Oct 21.Police said searches at rented premises in Greater Noida led them to three suspected firms. Investigators claimed that the firms were used to open bank accounts that were subsequently supplied to cyber fraudsters.Mishra allegedly said he, Bhadauriya, Verma and Pal had set up the firms and opened current accounts, which were handed over to Rana and Kumar for a monthly payment of Rs 25,000. The two allegedly supplied the accounts, along with banking kits and linked SIM cards, to Pandey, an MBA graduate.Pandey allegedly operated a bank account supply network and provided the accounts to individuals identified as Maxwell and Solitaire on a commission basis. Police said the two communicated through WhatsApp numbers bearing the US country code. The accounts were allegedly used to receive and route money obtained through cyber fraud.Mishra and Bhadauriya are BBA graduates, while Verma holds a BCA degree, Pal has an ITI qualification, and Rana and Kumar are BA graduates.Police seized 20 mobile phones, 45 SIM cards, 39 point-of-sale machines, 33 debit cards, 28 cheque books, 15 scanners and two laptops, besides banking documents.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: Instagram chases YouTube with a push for longer, widescreen videos
articles.summary: Instagram is announcing a big push into longform horizontal video, which the platform is calling “Features.” It’s also testing several other video features and has been expanding its TV app.
articles.body: Instagram is announcing a big push into longform horizontal video, which the platform is calling “Features.” Instagram boss Adam Mosseri has been against doing longform video on the platform “for a long time,” he says in a six-and-a-half-minute video (here’s the widescreen version) with VP of product Tessa Lyons, saying that “one of my concerns has been, how do we make sure that we keep Instagram not just about entertainment, but about connecting with friends. If you watch a longform video, that’s “it’s a lot of Reels, photos, and carousels that you might not have sent to a friend,” meaning less likes and shares. [Media: Now, though, the team is working on making shortform and longform video “symbiotic,” according to Mosseri, like podcasts or comedy specials that can be both long videos and broken up into shorter ones. The announcement of this widescreen video push also follows the launch of Instagram’s TV app late last year. That app launched first as a Reels-focused experience and as a pilot for Amazon Fire TV devices in the US, but it’s since expanded to Google TVs, Samsung TVs and Apple TV, and Instagram launched new features like the ability to watch Stories earlier this year. Mosseri also talked about the updates with creators Samir Chaudry and Colin Rosenblum, and their video includes some clips of how longform video will show up on the platform. [Media: Today, Features are expanding to the US in a small test and is in testing with some creators in Brazil, according to Instagram spokesperson Megan Buckley. Instagram is testing a few other video-focused features as well, including clips pointing to a long video, a way for creators to create a “series” of Reels, and improvements for live video discovery.

On the other side, Valkyries coach Natalie Nakase changed the starting lineup for Game 4, swapping Tiffany Hayes and Kaila Charles for Kayla Thornton and Cecilia Zandalasini. articles.title: Hasan Piker sues Scott Jennings for defamation
articles.summary: Progressive Twitch streamer Hasan Piker filed a defamation lawsuit against conservative CNN commentator Scott Jennings on Tuesday, accusing him of falsely cl...
articles.body:
Progressive Twitch streamer Hasan Piker filed a defamation lawsuit against conservative CNN commentator Scott Jennings on Tuesday, accusing him of falsely claiming Piker advocated for lynching Black Americans after airing an edited video of his remarks.

The 38-page lawsuit, filed in federal court in Washington, D.C., centers on an Aug. 11 episode of "The Scott Jennings Show," in which Jennings shared clips of Piker claiming he had said, "the USA should resume lynchings against Black people."

Piker, who threatened legal action in August over the claim and shared further context to the clips, alleges Jennings knowingly misrepresented sarcastic comments he made during his livestreams by turning it into an apparent endorsement of racial violence.

"Mr. Jennings did not merely mischaracterize something Mr. Piker said," the complaint reads. "He took a false, fabricated, and manipulated video of Mr. Piker, added a made-up quotation that Mr. Piker never uttered, and then made accusations that went beyond even what the manipulated footage purported to show."

During the August broadcast, Jennings warned Black voters to pay close attention before playing the clip, which included an on-screen caption attributing a statement, "Let's go back to a better time when lynchings were happening," to Piker.

Jennings later accused Piker of "calling for Black voters to be lynched" and referred to what he called "the Piker plan of returning our country to lynchings."

The original footage came from an October 2024 Twitch broadcast in which Piker was reacting to a debate between two Black political commentators — one liberal and one conservative. After the conservative participant criticized "woke DAs," Piker sarcastically suggested the commentator wanted to return to an era of racial discrimination and lynchings, according to the complaint.

"He said, 'We need more Klansmen, OK? Can we go back to a better time when lynchings were happening?'" Piker said during the stream in reaction to the commentator's argument.

Piker's attorneys argue that the edited video removed the words "He said," along with his laughter and surrounding commentary, to intentionally make it appear as though Piker was expressing his own beliefs rather than mocking someone else's.

The dispute emerged amid the Michigan Senate race , where the edited video was circulated to criticize progressive Democratic candidate Abdul El-Sayed over his association with Piker.

When Jennings posted the segment on the social platform X, he referred to Piker as El-Sayed's "best pal and campaign partner," before accusing him of supporting racial violence.

The post has received roughly 2.5 million views as of Tuesday, according to the lawsuit, and Jennings allegedly refused to retract his statements despite receiving a written demand from Piker's attorneys on Aug. 31.

Piker's legal team also says the accusations damaged his reputation and threatened his ability to earn money through streaming, advertising and sponsorships.

articles.title: Brewers vs. Rays live updates, World Series lineups, where to watch: Brewers one win from first championship in franchise history
articles.summary: The Brewers can sweep the Rays in the World Series with a win Tuesday.
articles.body: The Tampa Bay Rays have dug themselves into a deep, deep hole heading into Game 4 of the 2026 World Series, as the Milwaukee Brewers hold a 3-0 series lead and are one win from the first championship in franchise history. A win would also make Milwaukee the first team to sweep the World Series since the 2012 San Francisco Giants and the first to sweep both the League Championship Series and the World Series since the LCS became a best-of-seven in 1985.First pitch is set for 8 p.m. ET Tuesday at Tropicana Field in St. Petersburg, Florida.The Brewers continued their dismantling of the Rays with a 10-1 win in Game 3 on Monday. Starting pitcher Robert Gasser allowed just one hit over six scoreless innings, facing the minimum, and Milwaukee broke it open with an eight-run fifth inning to take a 10-0 lead. By the time Tampa Bay got on the board in the ninth, the damage had long been done.In Game 4, the Brewers will hand the ball to right-hander Dustin May (7-9, 4.70 ERA) with a chance to clinch. May's last start came in Milwaukee's lone loss this postseason, Game 3 of the NLDS against the San Diego Padres, in which he allowed 3 hits and 2 earned runs while striking out 3 over 3 innings.The Rays will counter with right-hander Griffin Jax (8-10, 3.53 ERA) with their season on the line. He'll hope to improve on his previous start against the Cleveland Guardians in the ALCS, in which he allowed 5 hits and 3 earned runs over 4 innings, including the go-ahead, two-run homer by Petey Halpin. Jax has a 6.00 ERA in six innings this postseason, including two in relief against the New York Yankees in the ALDS.Follow along with Yahoo Sports for live updates, highlights and more as the Rays host the Brewers in Game 4 of the World Series.

articles.title: Cucurella confiesa el futbolista del Atlético con el que se pegaría: "Saca lo peor de mí... Le reviento"
articles.standfirst: Marc Cucurella le asegura a Ibai Llanos que "reviento" a Álex Baena en un combate de boxeo y el futbolista del Atlético acepta el reto
articles.summary: Marc Cucurella le asegura a Ibai Llanos que "reviento" a Álex Baena en un combate de boxeo y el futbolista del Atlético acepta el reto
articles.body: Marc Cucurella, lateral del Real Madrid, le confesó a Ibai Llanos con quién se pegaría en la famosa 'La Velada del Año' que organiza el popular 'streamer'. "¿Si te tuvieras que pegar en una velada de boxeo, contra quién te pegarías?", le preguntó el famoso 'streamer' a Kylian Mbappé, Unai Simón, Ronaldo Nazario, David Raya, Luis Díaz, Luis Figo, Unai Simón y Marc Cucurella la alfombra roja de la Gala del Balón de Oro. Mpappé contestó que "conozco desde hace pocos meses tu evento y ahora sí lo conozco. ¿Contra quién participaría? Contra ti, pero te dejo ganar". Luis Figo contestó que se enfrentaría "con Ronaldo Nazario", y por su parte Ronaldo replicó que "estaría bien enfrentarse con Figo, no sabe nada de boxeo". "Llevo mucho tiempo entrenando boxeo. Me enfrentaría con cualquiera, tengo buenas manos", subrayó el mítico futbolista brasileño. Luis Díaz pelearía "con Daniel Muñoz, le daría unos cortitos", David Raya "con Rodri", Unai Simón "contra ti (Ibai Llanos), con el mordisco en la oreja". Marc Cucurella le contestó a Ibai Llanos que "cambiaría, la cobra la dejo en paz" y que en la velada de boxeo se enfrentaría a "Álex Baena". "Álex Baena es amigo mío, pero saca lo peor de mí", apuntó el defensa campeón del Mundial con España junto a Baena. "Le reviento", subrayó Cucurella. Álex Baena aceptó el reto pugilístico de Cucurella y contestó al futbolista del Real Madrid en Instagram: "Cuando quieras , sitio día y hora".

articles.title: Control de mago, vaselina y por la escuadra: Ibai 'rescata' al Marcelo más espectacular a sus 38 años
articles.standfirst: El creador de contenido 'fichaba' al brasileño para su último vídeo
articles.summary: El creador de contenido 'fichaba' al brasileño para su último vídeo
articles.body: Ibai Llanos lleva mucho tiempo consiguiendo lo imposible en el sector de la creación de contenido, pero en su último vídeo nos ha regalado un contenido increíble para los amantes del fútbol. El contexto es muy sencillo, un seguidor le pedía ayuda para ganar un partido en una de las peores ligas de Cataluña en cuanto a nivel, ya que ya el año pasado quedaban últimos y en los dos primeros partidos de la temporada también se les resistía la victoria. Pues bien, a Ibai Llanos no se le ocurría otra cosa que fichar a Marcelo para hacer que este equipo llamado Los Resbalados FC intentara llevarse los primeros tres puntos. La leyenda del Real Madrid ayudaba a los chicos con un mensaje de unión y equipo, pero su función, que era ganar el partido, la cumplió a la perfección aunque también tuvo tiempo para 'espabilar' a los chavales y echar alguna que otra bronca. Y sí, es cierto que, como decía el propio Marcelo, con 38 años las piernas no van como antes y el despliegue físico que vimos del brasileño no fue el más exigente, pero cuando la pelota llevaba a sus pies sentimos lo que tantas veces hemos sentido viendo jugar a la leyenda del fútbol. Con el marcador 0-2 un compañero recuperaba en la frontal y Marcelo, haciendo ver como si no costara nada, endosaba de primeras un latigazo a la derecha del portero imparable. Pero la verdadera magia llegaba después. Para empatar el encuentro Marcelo se inventaba una de sus jugadas. Conducía por el centro del campo y solo una bicicleta le bastaba para acomodarse el balón a su pierna izquierda y hacer un tiro directo a la escuadra derecha. Y para culminar la remontada el brasileño nos dejaba una acción al alcance de muy pocos. El portero sacaba en largo y tras un control perfecto se quedaba solo ante el guardameta rival, y como solo los genios hacen en un espacio tan corto, picaba el balón y remontaba un partido que parecía imposible, por lo menos, para los mortales como nosotros.

articles.body: Instagram is testing long-form videos (again) to lure in creatives from YouTube, but the platform hasn’t figured out how (or if) it’ll actually pay them. After Instagram head Adam Mosseri announced Features on Monday, creators immediately started voicing their complaints on Threads and Reddit about the lack of monetization opportunities, compared to the ad share and performance-based incentives provided by YouTube. Mosseri addressed the monetization concerns in a Threads post yesterday, saying “We understand the economics matter a ton, and are exploring multiple options to help long-form creators get paid.” It’s anyone’s guess what those solutions will look like. In one post on Threads, creator Sidneyraz (real name Sidney Raskind) said it feels like Mosseri and Meta are “just making fun of us” by not giving creators the ability to place long-form monetization ads into Features videos. “Y’all know how this works and you know how ad calls work and you know that long form creators need ad rev to survive but you’re ask[ing] them all to upload long form content for free just to live on your platform,” Raskind said. “That’s insane.” [Media: The new Features format is currently being tested by a small group of creators in the US and Brazil. Features videos can be up to 90 minutes long (compared to the 20-minute max for Reels), and seemingly focus on landscape content instead of vertical, making them a good fit for Instagram’s TV apps as it tries to snare our attention across more screens. Meta does have some limited monetization tools for Reels, but these don’t pay creators directly per view like YouTube does. “What’s funny about Instagram adding long-form video and reels that link to the long form is the complete lack of any sort of monetization,” tech creator M. Brandon Lee said on Threads. “Why should I post my long form there? What benefit does it bring me? I can’t even post links in my content to make affiliate income unless I PAY you to post a LIMITED number of links. I can’t get ad share revenue. You want more but don’t give more.” While some longer-form video creators on Facebook previously reported good earnings via its old ad revenue-sharing payout model, Meta retired this in 2024 when it switched to a performance-based system. The primary incentive to post a Features video is the reach of Instagram, but the tradeoff is knowing that Meta will use it to train its AI models. Google considers YouTube videos free game for AI training too, of course, but at least creators get paid by the platform. [Media: Speaking on a podcast with Samir Chaudry and Colin Rosenblum, Mosseri said introducing pre-roll or mid-roll ads is “going to be problematic from a user experience perspective,” and that it doesn’t make sense to scale up the small existing performance-based program because Meta spends more money on it than it makes back. “There are three ways you can get paid at a high level: you can get paid by the platform directly, you can get paid by a fan, and you can get paid by a brand. Right now how it works on Instagram primarily is that you get paid by brands, some people get paid by fans,” Mosseri said. “Creators don’t produce a lot more when we pay, compared to what they already create.”

articles.title: WNBA Finals: Dream rediscover 3-point stroke, force Game 7 after riding dominant first half to resurgent win over Valkyries
articles.summary: Behind Allisha Gray's five triples, Atlanta made 13 shots from beyond the arc on Thursday.
articles.body: Atlanta Dream guard Allisha Gray came out firing on Thursday in Game 6 of the WNBA Finals and finished with 23 points and five 3s in an 80-69 win over the Golden State Valkyries on Oct. 29 at State Farm Arena in Atlanta, Georgia. (AP Photo/Brynn Anderson)AP Photo/Brynn AndersonThe Atlanta Dream knocked down just six 3-pointers during their Game 5 defeat to the Golden State Valkyries in this year’s WNBA Finals. Karl Smesko’s team netted that many triples in the first quarter of Game 6 three days later on Thursday afternoon in front of a home crowd that was raucous as ever despite the much-discussed early tip-off.Atlanta’s first field goal was an Allisha Gray 3-pointer. That was a harbinger. The Dream went 6 of 8 from beyond the arc in the opening frame and wrapped the day with 13 makes from outside.Their 3-point barrage fueled an offensive resurgence. After scoring only 62 and 55 points in Games 4 and 5, both losses, the Dream piled up 32 in the first quarter alone, en route to a 17-point advantage. A 22-point second half from Gabby Williams inspired a late-game push from the Valkyries, but Gray’s fifth and final 3-pointer restored the Dream’s double-digit lead, and Atlanta forced the first Game 7 in WNBA Finals history with a series-tying 80-69 win.The winner-take-all game will be played Saturday at 8 p.m. ET in Golden State’s Chase Center. Both the Dream and Valkyries are one win away from their first WNBA title in franchise history.Gray, who has been battling through a left hand injury, finished with a team-high 23 points on Thursday. She shot 5 of 7 from 3-point land. Rhyne Howard was 4 of 6 from long range and wasn’t far behind Gray on the stat sheet, registering 21 points. Although Angel Reese shot just 5 of 18 from the floor, she scored 15 points — the total she combined for the previous two games — and, with 14 rebounds, she notched her fourth double-double of the series. That’s the second most double-doubles any player has recorded in a single WNBA Finals.Missed layups haunted Golden State in the early going. Williams wasn’t exempt from those struggles. Still, she persevered to mount a game-high 26 points and draw the Valkyries within eight points with 1:15 to go.Game 6 tipped off just after its expected start time of 12:30 p.m. ET. When and where exactly in Atlanta the matchup was going to be held was previously up in the air due to fan demand and scheduling complications, namely the fact that State Farm Arena — which seats approximately 13,500 more people than the Dream’s home venue but has hosted the team’s games throughout its postseason run — was already going to be the site of an Atlanta Hawks regular-season game Thursday night.So in order for the stadium to fit both games in on Thursday, Dream-Valkyries had to be played early, a controversial compromise. Dream ownership clarified this week that, months ago, as well as again during the playoffs, it raised concerns about schedule conflicts like this one. Those concerns, according to Dream ownership, “did not receive the attention, nor the urgency that they deserved.”There was no rushed championship celebration Thursday afternoon, however. The Dream stretched the series, keeping their title hopes alive.This story is being updated.

articles.title: Dakar Relocates to Portugal and Morocco for 2027
articles.summary: The Dakar Rally will leave Saudi Arabia for its 49th edition, running between Portugal and Morocco from January 9 to 23, 2027, before heading back to Saudi A...
articles.body:
The Dakar Rally will leave Saudi Arabia for its 49th edition, running between Portugal and Morocco from January 9 to 23, 2027, before heading back to Saudi Arabia in 2028 for its 50th anniversary. Organizers described the move as exceptional, citing the recent situation in Saudi Arabia, and said the Dakar Classic, the Dakar Future Mission 1000, and the Dakar Saudi Next Gen program will all follow the relocation.

The event opens the 2027 season of the FIA and FIM World Rally-Raid Championships and consists of a prologue followed by twelve stages. The Algarve stages the prologue and the opening special out of Loulé-Faro, using the 30,000-seat Algarve Stadium that staged the finish of the W2RC's second round last April under the Automóvel Club de Portugal. Morocco then carries eleven stages, with a rest day at Agadir.

The route covers 7,824 km in total, including 4,341 km of special stage across six bivouacs, a figure close to recent editions. Most daily specials range between 350 and 500 kilometers. The service park opens January 5 at Loulé-Faro, where administrative and technical scrutineering runs from January 6 to 8. After the prologue on January 9 and the first special stage the next day, competitors transfer to an overnight Mediterranean crossing to Nador, reaching Morocco on January 11 and transferring to the first bivouac at Bouarfa.

From the Oriental region in Morocco's northeast, the race heads south along the Atlas Mountains via Zagora and Agadir, then pushes into the far-southern deserts, with Smara and nearly Dakhla marking the second week's furthest points. The caravan returns north via Smara and the Atlantic coast before finishing in Marrakech.

Race Director David Castera called the edition "uncompromising" and said the organization has designed "a true Dakar" despite the short timeframe. "Competitors will discover the Kingdom from one end to the other," he said, pointing to Morocco's infrastructure and the ACP's support in Portugal.

Castera said 350 competitors have already registered. The event will once more reach broadcast audiences in more than 190 countries. "The adventure continues," he said, "as do preparations for the historic celebration of the 50th edition in Saudi Arabia."

articles.title: Harry Houdini returns for one final stunt this Halloween in Fox Nation special marking 100th death anniversary
articles.summary: AI-generated imagery brings Harry Houdini and his inner circle back to life in a groundbreaking Fox Nation documentary series spanning three episodes.
articles.body: Thanks to the latest technology, Harry Houdini is making his return from the grave — just in time for the 100th anniversary of his death. The new three-part Fox Nation series, "Houdini: Back from the Dead," uses artificial intelligence to revive the 20th-century entertainer and show audiences his life story and the death-defying stunts that defined a generation. "Ladies and gentlemen, one minute and 20 seconds, that's all they can find of my real voice," an AI-generated version of the acclaimed escape artist said in the show's introduction. "A scratchy recording, barely audible — but it is enough." OZZY OSBOURNE'S LATEST REINVENTION IS AN AI-POWERED INTERACTIVE HOLOGRAM EXPERIENCE The series conducted a mock interview with Houdini using advanced technology, asking him about his fears and the risk of accidents during his awe-inspiring tricks. "Showmanship is the largest factor in any act," the AI conjuring of Houdini said. "But the truth is, I've faced death hundreds, even thousands of times. For example, take the upside down. I'll never be able to make anything as dangerous or difficult. For its debut performance, I had to burl in — the danger is very real. I'm loaded into stirrups by my ankles and lowered in. The cover is made to fit tightly onto the steel frame, and then padlocked." CNN, NBC, CBS INTERVIEWING VIRAL AI 'ACTRESS' TILLY NORWOOD RAISES EYEBROWS AMONG CRITICS The series brings not just the legendary illusionist back to life, but also those closest to him — including his wife, mother, brother and friends — allowing them to recount his career, personal relationships and most daring feats. Red Rock Films, the production company behind the series, made Fox Nation history at the show's release as "Houdini: Back from the Dead" became the platform's first full-length, multi-episode production that relied entirely on AI-generated imagery. NEW FOX NATION DOCUMENTARY CHRONICLES 20-YEAR JOURNEY BEHIND ‘REAGAN’ FILM To create historically accurate visuals, filmmakers drew on more than 400 historic photographs and archival footage. Actors provided the movements, mannerisms, and performances of the historical figures, while technology transformed their appearances. "Fox Nation is breaking new creative ground by using emerging technology to bring one of history's most fascinating figures to life for a modern audience," Lauren Petterson, president of the platform, said in a press release.Houdini died exactly 100 years ago on October 31, 1926. One century later, fans can now gain new access to the passionate performer's life and legacy by subscribing to Fox Nation. articles.body: The Golden State Valkyries are the 2026 WNBA Champions, taking home the trophy in just their second year of existence. The Valkyries capped off a grueling Finals series with a thrilling 68-63 Game 7 victory. The win was fueled by a stellar performance from star forward Gabby Williams, who scored 28 points in the second half to lift Golden State to the trophy.THE GOLDEN STATE VALKYRIES ARE 2026 WNBA CHAMPIONS 🏆The Valkyries are the FASTEST WNBA franchise to win a title (two seasons) 🤯👏 pic.twitter.com/U6D3ZdpWX3— Yahoo Sports (@YahooSports) November 1, 2026 The league's first Finals Game 7 since expanding the playoff format last year lived up to the billing: Both teams traded leads in the low-scoring matchup, as things stayed very tight until the final seconds. But the Valkyries emerged triumphant in front of a packed, raucous crowd at Golden State's Chase Center — or Ballhalla, as it's affectionately known — on Halloween night.THAT'LL DO IT! 🙌IN JUST THEIR SECOND YEAR OF EXISTENCE, THE GOLDEN STATE VALKYRIES ARE CHAMPIONS OF THE WNBA 🏆 pic.twitter.com/GckMgbfKwj— USA Sports (@usasports) November 1, 2026 The Valkyries' defense showed up early, with Golden State holding the Dream completely scoreless for nearly six minutes to start the first quarter. But Atlanta finally broke through with a layup from Angel Reese at the 4:07 mark before going on a big run to get back into the game.The second quarter also saw a run from the Dream, who outscored Golden State 18-10 after keeping them quiet for more than five minutes. Atlanta then went into halftime with a 30-24 lead, after a hot 13-point quarter from Jordin Canada.The Valkyries picked up the pace in the third quarter, even as things stayed tight. Despite a very quiet start for the Valkyries beyond the arc, Williams hit three 3-pointers in a one-minute span. She finished with 15 points in the third quarter.Despite trailing, Atlanta refused to give up: A few points from Canada and Allisha Gray pulled the Dream even with the Valkyries within the final minutes. But Williams wasn't done. The forward hit a massive 3 with two minutes left to send the Ballhalla crowd into the stratosphere.GABBY WILLIAMS FROM THE PARKING LOT 🅿️🤯Williams pulls up from 31 FEET and knocks down another monster triple and Golden State leads by three with 2:10 left in Game 7! 🎯#WNBAonUSA 🏆 | Dream 💭 | Valkyries ⚔️ pic.twitter.com/qv9WUZpVKD— USA Sports (@usasports) November 1, 2026 The Dream still kept it close up down to the wire, with Gray hitting a clutch 3-pointer with 36 seconds left to get back within four points. Even as the Valkyries danced away, Atlanta executed its defense perfectly, along with two more free throws from Gray, to make it a three-point game, but Veronica Burton's late shots from the line sealed the deal.Williams finished with 30 total points, leading both teams in scoring, but her defensive presence, especially in the fourth quarter, was just as crucial to the team's win. She earned Finals MVP for her efforts.It was an electric end to an electric seven-game series, which proved leads don't matter, defense wins games and a two-year-old franchise can take it all the way to the top.The Dream, who have been to the Finals four times without picking up a trophy, once again end a season with heartbreak. But the Valkyries achieved glory, a massive victory for a team full of underrated players who now get to celebrate in front of its home crowd."All it took was good people. That's it. All we heard last year: 'We don't have no stars, we don't have no talent,' yeah, right," Williams said on the broadcast after the win. "We got winners. We got people who are ready to put their bodies on the floor to win the game. They don't care about scoring, they just want to play defense and rebound and do whatever it takes. We've just built a beautiful culture here."

articles.summary: Formula 1 returns this weekend, continuing its tour of the Americas with the second weekend of a triple-header in Mexico City. The Mexico City Grand Prix marks the 19th of a planned 23 rounds of the world championship.
articles.body: Kimi Antonelli has won the 2026 Formula 1 world drivers' championship, at 20-years old becoming the series' youngest title winner. Antonelli finished P3 at the Mexico City Grand Prix — the 19th of 23 rounds of the championship – where all he had to do was score points if nearest rivals Lewis Hamilton and George Russell won the race. Neither did so — despite Hamilton starting on pole position.Red Bull's Max Verstappen won, followed by Hamilton and Antonelli on the podium.Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez is a notorious circuit for not wanting pole position due to the longest run to the first corner on the calendar. That didn't necessarily play out cleanly Sunday as Hamilton held the edge into Turn 1, but a furious challenge from Ferrari teammate Charles Leclerc into the Turns 4-7 complex led to fireworks. THIS MOMENT! 😱Here is the first lap move from Leclerc on Hamilton, which is currently under investigation 👇#F1 #MexicoGP pic.twitter.com/IX0YtniiKo— Formula 1 (@F1) November 1, 2026 Leclerc emerged with the lead after cutting a corner, but the damage was done as Hamilton was left vulnerable to a pass from Verstappen and Leclerc being assessed a five-second penalty. Leclerc built the requisite gap before a round of pit stops, but Verstappen's crew got him out ahead of Leclerc on the track and in position for the win.Hamilton, who spent most of the first two-thirds of the race lamenting the incident with Leclerc, eventually got ahead of his teammate on a restart off a red flag caused by a suspension failure on Valtteri Bottas' car on Lap 48/71. Antonelli spent most of the afternoon cruising around in the top five, but a great standing restart saw him pip Leclerc similar to Hamilton. The Italian would hold on for a podium in his world championship-clinching victory.Mexico City Grand Prix resultsMax Verstappen, Red Bull Racing (race time not given)Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari +0.799Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes +4.006Charles Leclerc, Ferrari +10.707Lando Norris, McLaren +11.778George Russell, Mercedes +12.263Oscar Piastri, McLaren +19.475Franco Colapinto, Alpine +20.204Liam Lawson, Racing Bulls +20.899Pierre Gasly, Alpine +21.483Gabriel Bortoleto, Audi +22.041Isack Hadjar, Red Bull Racing +22.503Ryo Hirakawa, Haas +25.373Alex Albon, Williams +27.562Carlos Sainz, Williams +28.638Nico Hülkenberg, Audi +29.977Sergio Pérez, Cadillac +30.695Arvid Lindblad, Racing Bulls DNFOliver Bearman, Haas DNFFernando Alonso, Aston Martin DNFLance Stroll, Aston Martin DNFValtteri Bottas, Cadillac DNFHirakawa replaces OconHaas made a rather sudden shift mid-weekend on Saturday, promoting reserve driver Ryo Hirakawa to replace Esteban Ocon for the rest of the weekend.BREAKING: Haas confirm Ryo Hirakawa will make his F1 debut in the Mexico City Grand Prix, replacing Esteban Ocon for the remainder of the weekend#F1 #MexicoGP pic.twitter.com/u6HoaVuncL— Formula 1 (@F1) October 31, 2026 Ocon is a 10-season F1 veteran and one-time race-winner who has driven for Haas for the past two seasons. articles.title: YouTuber Druski is going to make exclusive content for Netflix
articles.summary: Netflix announced a multiyear deal with Druski, and he’ll create original content “exclusively” for the streaming service. The first show coming to Netflix is Collect & Praise on December 1st.
articles.body: Netflix today announced a multiyear deal with the YouTuber, comedian, and influencer Druski, and he’ll create original content “exclusively” for the streaming service. The announcement is the latest in Netflix’s efforts to bring creators onto the platform, having previously landed deals with YouTubers including Mark Rober, Ms. Rachel, and Good Mythical Morning. Druski’s first show coming to Netflix is Collect & Praise, a semi-scripted comedy series where Druski plays a megachurch pastor, and it will debut on December 1st. It will be the first of “several original projects” planned by Druski and his production company, 4LIFERS Entertainment, according to a press release. Netflix is also licensing other Druski series, including Coulda Been Love, Coulda Been Daddy, and Coulda Been Records Auditions. The announcement follows Netflix’s recent earnings, where it told investors not to worry even though users have been watching less. The company recently laid off around 1,000 employees, and chief content officer Bela Bajaria and film lead Dan Lin left the company.

articles.title: Why Peacock is making a huge bet on YouTube
articles.summary: NBCUniversal Media Group chairman Matt Strauss discusses the Olympics, the NFL, Peacock, Love Island, and channel rebundling.
articles.body: Today, I’m talking with Matt Strauss, who is now chairman of the NBCUniversal Media Group. This is Matt’s second time joining me on the show, and there’s been a whole lot of organizational and structural change at NBCU since the last time he and I spoke just two years ago — pure Decoder bait. First, about a month after Matt was on the show, Comcast spun off most of the NBCU cable channels into something called Versant. That’s when Matt’s title changed from heading up just the direct-to-consumer offering — meaning Peacock, plus some other streaming services — to heading up the whole thing, across all distribution. And now, Comcast is spinning off the NBCU business entirely into a whole new standalone company. --- [Image: Verge subscribers, don’t forget you get exclusive access to ad-free Decoder wherever you get your podcasts. Head here. Not a subscriber? You can sign up here. --- That’s a lot to have going on all at once! And meanwhile, it’s only just this year that Peacock became an actual profitable business at all — and it’s still pretty far away from being anything like the juggernaut that Netflix is. But what NBCU has, and what Peacock has, that the rest of the streaming industry is still trying to wrap its head around, is live sports. Sports are huge. They held up the cable industry for years, they held up broadcast, and now they’re the big thing that could make streaming a winner for NBC. One thing before we start: You’ll hear me ask Matt about the red company and the blue company. That’s just my way of getting Matt to talk about Netflix and Skydance, the company that now owns both Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery. I think he did a good job playing along. Before we get going, do me a favor and subscribe to Decoder on YouTube, where we put out new episodes every Monday and Thursday. Okay: Matt Strauss, chairman of the NBCU Media Group. Here we go. This interview has been lightly edited for length and clarity. Matt Strauss, you are the chairman of the NBCUniversal Media Group. Welcome back to Decoder. Thank you so much, Nilay. It’s great to be back. I am very excited to talk to you. There’s a lot going on in the media. It is a tumultuous time in Hollywood. I have to tell the audience that you and I are speaking minutes after Anthropic filed its S-1, and all of humanity is going to be turned into AI. Who knows what entertainment we’ll be watching in the future? There’s a lot going on. Let’s start at the very beginning of this. You have a new job since last time you were on the show. Last time, you were the head of Direct-to-Consumer — you were basically the head of Peacock and the other apps inside the family. Now you’re the chairman of NBCUniversal Media Group. What’s the new job? What does that mean? NBCUniversal Media Group is comprised of certain services within NBC. It’s the broadcast network, it’s Bravo, it’s Peacock, it’s NBC Sports. We also have NBC News and Telemundo. One of the things that we recognized, especially when we spun off some of our cable assets last year into Versant, was that the assets we had truly worked better together. NBC has been like a megaphone. Given the reach of NBC, it’s been incredibly strategic in growing Peacock, which is a bit ironic because I think so many people believed that broadcasting was a bit of a relic of the past in this digital world, but it’s actually proven to be the opposite. As things have gotten more fragmented, having a broadcast network is actually a superpower because we’re continuing to see ratings growth. That has been really helpful as we’ve been building out Peacock. But actually, Peacock was also finding new audiences, like cord cutters or people who maybe didn’t grow up watching NBC or some of our cable networks. So, Peacock’s also been really strategic in reaching and driving people back to NBC and Bravo. So, I think that flywheel is where we recognized that we needed to start operating differently. I’ve been a huge advocate of what I like to call “centers of excellence” in how I like to structure the business, which is, content first and platform second. How do we get maximum reach, maximum engagement? That really required us thinking differently about how we were running the business. Essentially, instead of having a programming group within broadcast and a programming group within streaming, we just collapsed the business. Now you’ve got one programming team, one marketing team, one product and technology team, one decision sciences and research team, and one advertising team. They’re all incentivized around continuing to grow the portfolio, get that maximum reach, maximum engagement, and drive top-line revenue. I think that structure, which we put in place about 18 months ago, is contributing to a lot of the success that we’re seeing now. Even if you look at 2026, NBC is the number one network in total viewers. We had an unbelievable early part of the year with “Legendary February,” which you might remember. That’s when we had the Super Bowl, the Milan Cortina Olympics, and the NBA All-Star Game. In 17 days, we reached over 225 million viewers. This summer, we had Love Island, which was the number one show of the summer for streaming. You had the World Cup, which was the number one Spanish-language sporting event in US history on Telemundo and Peacock. We had a show called The Five-Star Weekend, which was our number one scripted drama. Now, we’ve led ourselves into the fall, where we have Sunday Night Football, which has been the number one show for 15 consecutive years. We had a great kickoff with over 25 million viewers. We just had the NBA tip-off last week with the Knicks and the Sixers, which is the number one rated tip-off in NBA history. So, it does feel like we’re firing on all cylinders in how we’re trying to operate with this, again, content-first-platform-second mantra. But just to go one level deeper, a big part of this strategy is figuring out how do we move audiences across platforms. For example, when I mentioned that Love Island was the number one streaming show of the summer, 40 percent of those Love Island viewers also tuned in to watch the World Cup. So, migrating viewers back and forth across the portfolio is a critical part of how we see ourselves continuing to grow. But to effectuate that, you need to structure yourself in a way where people are incentivized along that vision. We’re still evolving as an organization, but I’m really proud of some of the milestones and accomplishments that we’ve made as a team. I love my job. I feel like I’ve got the best job in the industry at the moment. It is a tumultuous time in Hollywood, and you seem like one of the happiest people in the industry right at the second. That is very notable. You’re a Decoder pro, you brought up structure. I’m dying to ask you about the Decision Sciences Group. That’s the other question I ask everybody. But let me just back out for one second. You’re describing quite a lot of freedom in rethinking how something like NBCUniversal would work. You mentioned the Versant spin, so CNBC, MS Now, and a bunch of channels went that way. I’m on its networks all the time. I would describe the folks at Versant as feeling more free. They’re disconnected from the battleship that was Comcast and NBCUniversal. They can go try whatever they want to try. They’re energized by it in some ways. Then, Comcast looked at NBCUniversal and said, “We’re going to spin off that off as well. We’re going to be the cable business and NBCUniversal will be the entertainment business, and now you’re in charge of that.” You’re like a 20-year Comcast veteran. I think you got your start doing cable boxes. Yep. I started in 2004 at Comcast. Just tell me about that process. We spun off CNBC and MS Now into Versant. Now we’re looking at this company. We ought to spin off NBCUniversal as well. Just tell me about how that came about. What was that moment like? Did you all sit in a boardroom? Did it come down from on high? How did that happen? Well, that decision really was made by Brian Roberts and Mike Cavanagh. Candidly, I was not in the room when that decision was made, but I think if you were to ask people at NBCUniversal, it makes strategic sense. Do you feel that same sense of freedom? You know what? I think that there’s an energy. When people show up here, they feel very passionate about what they do. They believe in our strategy, they believe in our portfolio. Look at NBCUniversal more broadly. Before, I was describing the Media Group, but that is one piece of the broader company. You have Universal Pictures and Universal Television, which have obviously been having an unbelievable summer with The Odyssey and Obsession. You’ve got Universal’s theme parks and experiences. We opened up Epic Universe last year. We opened up a kids theme park in Texas. We announced we’re going to open up a theme park in the UK. We have Sky, which was part of the company but more squarely sat within Comcast Cable. Now that’s going to migrate over to the new NBCUniversal as part of this restructure. Then, you have these media assets, which I spoke about earlier. So, you’ve got this unbelievable portfolio. I think that people here really believe in our growth and that if we’re a separate company, it’s going to allow us to move faster. It’s going to let us have more clarity around where we want to make capital allocations and decisions. There are a few areas that really play to our strengths as an organization. One of them is live sports and live events. That’s always been a part of NBCUniversal that we’re really known for. If you just look at the sports portfolio that we have, Nilay, we’ve got NFL, NBA, MLB, the Big Ten Conference, the Premier League. We’ve got the Olympics with the IOC. You’ve got this unbelievable portfolio of sports content, and that’s a strategic asset when we’re partnering with the leagues because we believe in broadcast. We believe in broad reach. We’re not trying to put everything exclusively on a streaming platform. In 2026, we’ve demonstrated across almost every single sport that we can actually continue to grow ratings and reach new audiences, which is something that’s becoming more and more complicated. Can I ask about that? Because you also run Peacock, which is a paid streamer where you can access sports. When you say grow ratings on broadcast, are more people putting up antennas to watch sports over the air? No. What I mean... By the way, about 20 percent of TV households in this country do still use over-the-air antennas as— Oh, we have lots of listeners who are going to tell you that’s the best picture quality you can get. You should really think of it more as an entertainment platform designed to maximize share of time and retention. I think the partnership we announced with YouTube this summer is going to be an example of how we see ourselves continuing to drive more of that audience and engagement across our platform but also working very closely with YouTube. That YouTube deal looks like the rebundling you’re talking about, right? Peacock will be available to YouTube Premium subscribers. I have YouTube TV. I imagine that will somehow connect the dots. YouTube is fascinating because it has the user-generated content platform and TV. Those things are starting to compete with each other, right? I look at the viewership charts, and classic, user-generated YouTube is skyrocketing, just eating up everyone’s time all day long. Everyone has to be there. I’m assuming the economics of YouTube TV look like cable for you. They have to be far more lucrative. When you go into a room with [YouTube CEO] Neil Mohan and say, “Well, there’s the platform that’s very lucrative and there’s a platform I have to be on,” how do you reconcile the economics of the two? From my point of view, it’s not one or the other. It’s both. It comes back to what I said about how they’re not exactly the same audiences. There’s some overlap, but somebody who is subscribing to YouTube TV is not necessarily the same person who is subscribing to YouTube Premium or consuming content on main YouTube. I agree with you that when you look at this through the share of time lens, YouTube has done an unbelievable job creating a platform and business model that allows it to continue to grow. I don’t see anything that would indicate that’s going to slow down. When you look at it from my point of view, so much of our content and IP lives on YouTube in some form, whether it’s SNL or Love Island, whether it’s clips from The Traitors or any of our NBC shows. But those viewers don’t necessarily subscribe to Peacock. They don’t necessarily watch NBC or Bravo. So, I think that was the opportunity. That was the unlock. How actually can we transform ourselves to reimagine what it could look like to partner with YouTube? One of the things that I was talking about earlier with this great rebundling — which we talked about and somewhat predicted seven years ago — was that the one thing that held the bundle together in cable television for many years was sports. What you don’t want to do is a bundle deal without getting the right underlying wholesale economics. What will happen is that you could take a very high ARPU, direct-to-consumer subscriber and end up cannibalizing them for a low, wholesale bundled subscriber. What you’re really looking for is incrementality. Is this going to drive incremental subscribers, and can I get the right wholesale economics where this is also incremental on the revenue side? What’s interesting about YouTube is that I think it’s a win-win. It’s a win-win because there’s multiple components to this deal. One aspect is that there’s going to be a bundle launched next year with the ad-supported tier of Peacock and a tier of YouTube Premium. Now, you’re going to get access to all of the benefits of YouTube Premium with the ad-supported version of Peacock. We believe that these are mostly incremental subscribers, or people who do not necessarily have Peacock today. So, it’s going to grow Peacock while adding more value to YouTube Premium. My prediction is that if you and I have a conversation a year from now, Peacock will be one of the top distributed streaming services in the United States. Do you care that you don’t own your last-mile customer that way? This was a big reason everyone went to streaming. They were selling their content to Netflix, and they realized Netflix owned the customer. Now we’ve all got to stand up our own streaming services because we want to own the customer and the cable bundle is falling apart. Do you care now that as you rebundle, YouTube will own the customer in some important way? I think that when you say “own the customer,” really what you’re talking about is, “How do I get the ability to personalize the experience so that I could super-serve an individual both with content and with advertising? What’s ultimately going to create the monetization engine that we need?” I was describing the value of Peacock and the fact that 80 percent of our subs are on the ad platform and that we typically charge premium CPMs (cost per mille) because we have this ability to super-serve our fandoms and franchises, and we have the data to do it. I think that the relationship with YouTube that we announced this summer is going to allow us to have a much deeper integration with YouTube on the data side as well as the integration with FreeWheel. So, we’re at a point where we’re almost indifferent again about where somebody consumes the content— FreeWheel is your programmatic advertising business. Yes. That was a critical part to this unlock with YouTube because we can create a bundle that is going to drive incremental subscribers and value. To your point, YouTube TV is the fastest-growing pay TV distributor. I think the pay TV ecosystem has been declining at a 6-7 percent CAGR. Over the past five years, YouTube TV has grown at a 26-27 percent CAGR. It has over 10 million subscribers and are likely going to be the number one pay TV distributor in the next couple of years. We extended our linear portfolio agreement with YouTube TV, which is going to provide us stability and growth on that part of our portfolio as well. What we were just describing around having a much deeper integration with the data, analytics, and targeting is going to allow us to monetize our inventory. It’s all of these pieces. We think this is an example of how we’re trying to think differently, or how we’re trying to be innovative and identify strategic partners. I don’t know if the red company or the blue company would be in a position to do the kind of deal that I’m describing, but it’s precisely because we are independent and looking to be more flexible. I think that actually becomes a calling card for how we could work with other companies in a way that is really transformative. Let me ask you, I think the red company hypothetically got turned upside down because it relied on data too much for the programming and now it’s going to change a bunch of programming executives, so we’ll see where it goes. The hypothetical blue company led by the hypothetical son of a billionaire is out in the market. It made a big content acquisition. He’s saying, “Oh, we’re going to invest in technology and we’ll compete with Northern California. We’ll compete with any of the platforms based on our technology bet.” To me, that seems like an old story where I know the ending. Trying to run at TikTok’s technology without the content is just going to get you backwards. If you were running the blue company, how would you think about technology in that way? Well, I’m going to answer the question based on how I’m running our company. The blue company’s new. Anything could happen with the blue company. I think my answer, though, would not change depending on where I sat within this industry. I believe that we need to be an open ecosystem, that you’ve got to go where the viewers are. That’s what led us to make a lot of strategic decisions, whether it’s the deal that I just described with YouTube, or the channel deals for the ad-free tier of Peacock with Amazon and Roku. We’ve done bundling deals. We’ve done a bundle deal with Apple. We’ve done a bundle deal with Walmart. You’re trying to give consumers choices. Everything I’ve done in my career has always been around the north star of giving consumers choice: what they want, when they want, where they want. That, to me, has been the mantra for how we’re trying to build our company. All of that being said, I am still also a huge believer in the product, the technology, and the experience. You may be able to watch the Olympics on another platform through NBC or Peacock, but I truly believe the best experience was on Peacock. Are you allowed to say that on other people’s networks? Can you go on to Amazon channels and say, “This is great, but if you want the first class, get out of this app and open Peacock?” Do they let you say that? Well, I wouldn’t say it that way, though. First of all, I think when somebody subscribes to Peacock, they should be able to access our service regardless of the platform. In that respect, we do cross-authentication — meaning you can subscribe and watch on Peacock, or you could subscribe and access our service through channels. I’m not here to tell the consumer what the best experience is. I think that we lead by example. The consumers vote based on where they ultimately decide to engage. If you want to get access to some of these cool features that I’m describing, if you want to play a game that we created, or if you want to listen to a podcast, or… I’ll give you another example. We’re testing our membership program because we shouldn’t think of viewers as subscribers, we should think of them as members. What are the other values that you can get as part of being a member? Well, maybe some of those values could be based on your tenure or your level of engagement. Maybe you get discounts to NBC merchandise. Maybe you get special access when you go to Universal theme parks. Maybe you get discounts from some of our advertising partners, like Domino’s. How do we start to add more value? But maybe that membership is only available when you’re on our platform. I think of it more as needing to give consumers the choice. At the same time, we are investing in product and technology and on experiences that are really meant to be delivered upon the platform that we have created. We’ve got an unbelievable team, in my opinion, that has created a best-in-class, scalable platform that not only powers Peacock, but also powers Sky’s Now TV. It’s the same platform that we’ve also distributed to dozens of countries around the world. We’ve got a world-class team that is really trying to transform, surprise, and delight viewers in a way that I’m not sure other platforms are going to be able to do around our content and franchises, especially when it comes to especially these major tentpole events. I want to end by asking maybe the most important question of all. We’re talking a lot about internet-distributed businesses and consumers signing up for services and being able to churn and quit. There are a lot of free market dynamics there, which I think are very powerful and very important. That means you get to program whatever you want to program. You have chosen live in sports and, importantly, you mentioned news at the top of this conversation. NBC News is part of this portfolio. NBC News is also distributed over broadcast. It’s distributed over the air. The Trump administration and FCC Chairman Brendan Carr, in particular, has expressed a lot of desire to pressure broadcast networks because you use the public spectrum, particularly news networks. He’s withheld the broadcast licenses for ABC stations, for example. He has threatened the other broadcast networks. There’s a lot of pressure on NBC News. How are you handling that? Are you pushing back? Because that is the one place where you’re not allowed to just do whatever you want, right? The government gets to tell you what to say in an increasingly uncomfortable way. Yeah. Look, I think I give a lot of credit to [NBCUniversal News Group Chairman] Cesar Conde and the NBC News organization who are big believers in freedom of speech and freedom of the press. I think they’re doing a fantastic job. When it comes to distribution of our content, especially our news programming, I think that’s an example where it’s available everywhere. I mean, we truly make it available not only on Peacock, NBC, and over the air, but through Fast TV, NBC News Now— Have you made this argument to the administration? Because I’ve met a lot of FCC chairmen over the years, and until Carr showed up, the argument they would make is that we have to get away from overthinking broadcast because the audience is everywhere, and they don’t actually make a distinction between broadcast television and cable. That was a Republican talking point for years and years. This is nonsense. The other version is that everyone’s on TikTok and the industry has to contend with that in some way. We should get more people internet access because that will actually even the playing field. Now we’ve come to, “You have to use the spectrum in the public interest.” It is different and the government should impose some speech pressure — which again, I think is inappropriate — but that is a new argument. I’m wondering if you have said to the administration, “Look, the consumer doesn’t make this distinction and we as a company aren’t making this distinction.” Well, I’ve not had those direct conversations myself. Obviously, we have a government affairs team that works very closely with regulators in DC. There’s probably no better time to be alive than right now when it comes to being able to access content through multiple modalities, whether it’s over-the-air broadcast, social media platforms, or free. If you were to look at Peacock, not only do we distribute NBC News, we distribute all of our own stations as well. I could be watching the Los Angeles local news in New York or I could be watching the Philadelphia local news. There’s no shortage of ways that we are supporting the public good in giving them multiple ways and choices in how they want to consume and access their news programming, and I don’t think that’s going to change. I think we’re going to continue to advocate for freedom of speech and freedom of the press. I think our news organization has been doing an unbelievable job in the product and the service that they’re doing for the public. Yeah. Matt, you can tell that’s an important topic for me for a lot of reasons. What’s next for NBCUniversal Media Group? What’s next for Peacock? What should people be looking for? I think what’s next for NBCUniversal Media Group is, as we talked about, we will likely be a separate company as part of the new NBC this time next year. You’ve got to come back. There’s a bunch of questions where I knew I wasn’t going to get answers because the deal isn’t closed yet. When that closes, you’ve got to come back because I have a million questions. I will definitely come back. I’m really looking forward to it. I think the other piece, as you know, is that we had our Q3 earnings last week. We talked a lot about Peacock and how we had a very different strategy with Peacock from the others when we launched our service six years ago. I’m really proud to share that Peacock was profitable in Q3 for the second consecutive quarter. We had $261 million of EBITDA. That’s $470 million better year-over-year. I think the team has done an unbelievable job, and I feel really good about our momentum and continuing to grow. It’s good proof that there’s not one way to go to market. There’s not one strategy or approach. You’ve got to play your hand and to your strengths, and you’re going to see us continue to do that at NBCUniversal. Yeah. We didn’t even talk about what AI might do to the cost structure of video. When you come back, we’re going to get into it. Matt, thank you so much for being on Decoder. Thank you so much. Questions or comments? Hit us up at decoder@theverge.com. We really do read every email! Decoder with Nilay Patel A podcast from The Verge about big ideas and other problems. SUBSCRIBE NOW!

articles.title: One of Google’s Android partners turned 1.3 million set-top boxes into a botnet
articles.summary: Google says it dismantled the backdoor of one of its manufacturing partners used to create a botnet including 1.3 million Android TV devices.
articles.body: Google says one of its Android manufacturing partners secretly built a backdoor in 1.3 million devices and turned them into a botnet. The company says it has now dismantled the backdoor and “cut ties” with the manufacturer, the Shenzhen, China-based Videostrong Technology Co., which has been banned from building or selling certified Android devices or supplying software for them. The infected devices were used without owners’ knowledge for “malicious activity,” like ad fraud, data exfiltration, and routing unauthorized network traffic. Google claims the “backdoor and botnet were intentionally developed, deployed, and operated for financial gain,” saying: > Videostrong monetized the backdoor by selling access to criminal affiliates and loading those affiliates’ malware modules onto infected devices. These secondary modules were conducting ad-fraud; silently enrolling infected devices into residential proxy networks; and loading additional malware onto XCPE-compromised devices. We also took action to disrupt the command and control (C2) domains that operate these affiliate modules. Because these affiliates each have diversified distribution channels for their modules beyond XCPE, we assess that taking down their C2 domains will sever access to at least 10 million additional compromised devices. It wasn’t just one device that was impacted, either — the malware was found “built directly into many different device models and brands over multiple years.” Most of those were Android TV set-top boxes, but the botnet also infected other “Android-based IoT devices, including telehealth devices, karaoke machines, and digital signage devices.” Google says Videostrong used “obfuscation techniques” to load the malware onto users’ devices after they booted up the hardware for the first time. Google also says it made changes to its review process for device manufacturers after this incident.

articles.title: Caleb Williams' late push, Jeffery Simmons' dominance help Bears hold off Seahawks for big prime-time victory
articles.summary: Chicago doused a late Seattle spark with big plays on both ends of the field.
articles.body: SEATTLE — The Chicago Bears emerged triumphant in a big NFC matchup against the Seattle Seahawks on Monday night. Despite a late score that pulled the Seahawks within three points, Caleb Williams stayed cool to get a late touchdown, while the Bears' defense did enough to stifle the spark in a 34-17 victory. Chicago got things started early, silencing the crowd at Lumen Field with a methodical, 17-play opening drive that ended in Williams finding Luther Burden III in the end zone on a 1-yard touchdown pass. Seattle's offense, meanwhile, spent the first half struggling, and Chicago's new defensive acquisition Jeffery Simmons played a role in that. He notched his first sack as a Bear in the Seahawks' second series of the game, bringing down Sam Darnold for a 6-yard loss. He finished with six tackles, two for loss and one pass deflection. The Seahawks regained their footing enough in the second quarter. Chicago led 13-3, but in the final seconds of the half, Sam Darnold found Jaxon Smith-Njigba for a masterful (and much-needed) 43-yard touchdown that cut Seattle's deficit to 13-9. Watch him woooork 🙂‍↕️ @jaxon_smith1 Seattle Seahawks (@Seahawks) November 3, 2026 The Bears didn't back down, though, breaking up a slow third quarter with another touchdown and blocking a Seahawks field-goal attempt early in the fourth.Seattle bounced back on the next drive with when DeMarcus Lawrence forced and recovered a Bears fumble. That gave the Seahawks a chance that they capitalized on. Darnold found wideout Cooper Kupp in the end zone for a 7-yard score, and connected with Tory Horton for a 2-point conversion to pull the game within 20-17.That bit of momentum didn't last long. Williams cooly led the Bears down the field for a touchdown, converting on third-and-9 (thanks to a delay-of-game call that actually might've saved the drive) on a 39-yard quick toss to Kalif Raymond that was officially counted as a rushing attempt. Kalif Raymond turned on the burners 💨📺: ESPN pic.twitter.com/iFUiG5Priz— Chicago Bears (@ChicagoBears) November 3, 2026 D'Andre Swift then pulled through for a 5-yard touchdown run to push the lead back up to double digits.A tipped interception on Darnold then dashed any last hopes of a Seahawks comeback, especially with Swift taking in another touchdown, his third of the night.He finished with 69 yards on 27 carries, which wasn't efficient, but the three scores mattered more. Seattle had one last futile drive, but turned it over on downs on fourth-and-4 from the Chicago 7. That was enough for the Bears to seal the victory.

articles.title: Netflix will show you themed recommendations through a new ‘AI Discover’ tab
articles.summary: Netflix’s TV app is getting a new “AI Discover” tab where the company will show experimental, AI-powered features to help you find new shows and movies to watch.
articles.body: Netflix’s TV app is getting a new “AI Discover” tab where the company will show experimental, AI-powered features to help you find new shows and movies to watch. The first of these experiments surfaces content based around themes, like “Something Light,” “Family Movie Night,” or “Quick Watches.” When you pick a theme, Netflix will show you recommendations that match it. If you don’t like a recommendation, you can tell that to Netflix, and the app will remember it. The company says that AI Discover is powered by “a new intelligence layer we’ve been building that responds to what members tell us in real time and keeps learning.” AI Discover, which will show up as a “Discover” tab along your top menu, is gradually starting to roll out in the US to “members who use Netflix in English on supported TVs.” The announcement follows Netflix recently laying off around 1,000 employees as growth has slowed and users are reportedly watching the service less.

articles.title: Canva is announcing changes and layoffs affecting 22 percent of its staff
articles.summary: Canva is making significant changes affecting 1,271 people, which is 22 percent of its staff, co-founder and CEO Melanie Perkins announced today.
articles.body: Canva is making significant changes affecting 1,271 people, which is 22 percent of its staff, co-founder and CEO Melanie Perkins announced today. “For some people, this will mean changes to their roles or being asked to relocate to centralised hubs,” says Perkins. “Sadly, it will also mean saying goodbye to teammates and friends who have helped build Canva into what it is today.” In her note to staff, Perkins says that: > After exploring a wide range of alternatives, I’ve come to the difficult conclusion that small changes won’t be enough. To set ourselves up for the next decade, we need to refound Canva, getting back to our roots of small, empowered teams with the freedom to make decisions, take ownership and focus on what matters most for our community. Canva’s changes include bringing its Product, Growth, and Platform teams together into one product organization, “simplifying layers” and “consolidating overlapping responsibilities,” and making Sydney the “primary home for more of our product teams, as well as roles in other Specialties where shared context and close collaboration are especially important.” Starting in January, Canva will also “expect” most hybrid employees to spend 2 to 3 days in an office each week “depending on what makes sense in your area.” Employees leaving Canva will get benefits including at least six months of salary, twelve months of healthcare coverage, and career support resources. Yesterday, Squarespace announced layoffs affecting 19 percent of its staff.

articles.body:
Dalton Knecht 's time with the Los Angeles Lakers ended earlier this month after the team waived him. The former first-round pick has since joined the New York Knicks on a two-way contract and has had to wait for his first opportunity with his new team.

That chance came on Wednesday against the Chicago Bulls, and Knecht made the most of it . He scored 10 points and grabbed seven rebounds in 16 minutes as New York cruised to a 135-105 win.

The 24-year-old shot 4-of-6 from the field and made two 3-pointers. His first basket came on a powerful putback dunk, followed by a step-back 3-pointer in the final seconds of the first half.

articles.title: You can edit your videos with AI on Instagram’s new desktop Edits app
articles.summary: Instagram launched Edits, its standalone video editing app, on macOS with a feature that allows users to edit their content with a connected AI agent.
articles.body: Instagram’s standalone video editing app is now available on macOS, where you can plug in your AI agent of choice to assemble your videos. Instagram’s Matthew Simari, head of product management for Edits, said in an interview with The Verge, “One of the things we’re releasing with Edits Desktop is a MCP for all the tools within Edits Desktop. You can use any agent you want, you can use Muse — we would love you to — but really any agent you want of [your] choice, to edit, tweak, work with your video.” The Edits app originally launched on mobile platforms last year. Simari said creators have been “heavily” requesting a desktop version, but AI plans were also a factor in the expansion to macOS. Instagram added an AI “creative assistant” to the mobile version of Edits in September, which can give users video suggestions and feedback using data and metrics from their Instagram account like views and retention on their videos. On the new desktop version of Edits, Simari said users can “go back and forth from agentic to manual editing.” He gave an example of a creator asking Meta’s Muse agent to use the Edits MCP to make a rough cut of a video in their downloads folder, saying, “It’ll be able just to go access that MCP, do the tool calls, make that rough cut for you, and then you can open that project file in Edits to continue editing.” [Image: [Image: [Image: The jump to desktop follows Instagram’s push into longform, widescreen videos which tend to be a lot easier to edit on a larger screen. Meta says it’s “expanding Edits to support multiple aspect ratios” and adding support for watermark-free 4K exports. Beyond its AI features, the desktop version of Edits also has more advanced editing features like a full multi-track timeline and precise audio waveforms and color grading tools. It also supports keyboard shortcuts, which Meta says can be “carried over from another editor.” Like the mobile Edits app, the desktop version has access to Instagram’s audio library and support for publishing videos directly to Instagram. Meta also says audio and text styles users have saved in the mobile app will be accessible from the desktop version, too. However, the desktop app currently isn’t available on Windows or Linux, only macOS. You can’t edit the same project across both mobile and desktop yet, either. Meta says it’s working on cross-platform editing, and plans to update the new desktop app weekly.
